doc.title: Jimmy Owens — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Studio work, Herbie Mann and recording
title: Frost show personnel and being the youngest in the band
summary: Maxine reads out the Frost band members; Owens recalls always being the youngest, including in Hampton's Golden Men of Jazz.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: I have a photo here of the Billy Taylor band. David Frost show, 1969­ 1972. [It was] Bobby Thomas on drums, Bob Cranshaw on bass George Burg…
Yeah, Bob left after a couple of months and he was replaced by Wilbur Bascomb, who worked he rest of the show.
… Jimmy Owens, Dick Hurwitz on trumpet, and Morty Bullman on trombone.
Morty Bullman was a very fine trombonist who worked with the Arthur Godfrey Show, had done all these things. He was Carmine Caruso’s first brass student, okay? This was in the early 50’s.

Yes, I was always the youngest in the band, always the youngest. When Clark Terry called me, he said, “Jimmy, I need you to go these two gigs for me.” I became the youngest again with Lionel Hampton and his Golden Men Of Jazz. I was the youngest in that band and I did those two or three gigs with Lionel Hampton.
